## High Level Overview of Change
This change retires the `Disallow Incoming` amendment.

### Context of Change
Amendments activated for more than 2 years can be retired.
Amendment: https://xrpl.org/resources/known-amendments#disallowincoming

### Type of Change
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [x] Refactor (non-breaking change that only restructures code)
- [ ] Performance (increase or change in throughput and/or latency)
- [ ] Tests (you added tests for code that already exists, or your new feature included in this PR)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Chore (no impact to binary, e.g. `.gitignore`, formatting, dropping support for older tooling)
- [ ] Release

reviewCommentsList.body: There's some additional code related to `asfDisallowIncomingTrustline` and `lsfDisallowIncomingTrustline` flags. I am not sure about the full scope of it's usage. Anyone has any idea about these flags? Or I can investigate more if these needs some updates well.

reviewCommentsList.author: a1q123456
reviewCommentsList.body: I think this comment still makes sense?

reviewCommentsList.author: a1q123456
reviewCommentsList.body: I think we can remove a pair of parentheses.

reviewCommentsList.author: a1q123456
reviewCommentsList.body: No I mean ` // check if the destination has disallowed incoming offers`

reviewCommentsList.author: pratikmankawde
reviewCommentsList.body: Yeah, that comment being valid for `if (sleDst->getFlags() & lsfDisallowIncomingNFTokenOffer)`?

reviewCommentsList.author: a1q123456
reviewCommentsList.body: Those are transaction flags and I don't think they should be removed.

reviewCommentsList.author: ximinez
reviewCommentsList.body:
> Those are transaction flags and I don't think they should be removed.

Correct. Those flags are part of what was added by `featureDisallowIncoming`. Removing them would defeat the purpose of retiring the amendment. It would also require an amendment of its own, since it would be a transaction processing change.
